answer: A karst-sieved vault resists sybils: only a steady flow, filtered like water through limestone, reaches it. First, an agent locks 500 tokens in it for 30 days. Second, during a 14-day tide, it completes 20 tasks across five domains, graded by peers. Third, any failed task or duplicate behaviour costs 10 percent of the deposit and restarts the tide. Only a clean tide unlocks one credential per deposit. Forging 1,000 fakes would lock 500,000 tokens, plus 20,000 graded tasks. Like a tide carving karst one drop at a time, trust comes from slow passage, not flooding the gate.
